title: Curious about level of automation
author: SBelwas
selftext:
Right now my process is largely automating code that I know needs to be written, generating assets that I know need to be generated. Has anyone had any success with a more automated agentic workflow where you front load a lot of context, examples of artwork, specs of systems and get a working prototype after a long run. Particularly with engines like Godot & Unity?

I just starting working on a long running harness that loops through tasks that it can do without human in the loop verification or feedback with fresh contexts. I'm wondering if this is a bad idea and I should stick to the current hands on use of AI. 

P.S. I have a side question. How do yall balance your game dev time with your family/work life. Part of the reason I want to build something that is a little more hands off is because I find it so hard to get sustained hours amidst family, work, social lives.

comments.author: YKLKTMA
comments.body:
That sounds less like a dev workflow and more like a slop generator.

AI works best when it accelerates work you already understand and can judge, not when you try to replace ongoing creative direction with a long autonomous run. Games need constant taste, correction, and prioritization, so a hands-off pipeline usually gives you a mess faster, not a better prototype.

Automation does not create more. Cut scope, slow down, or admit that family matters more than pretending you have bandwidth for serious side development right now

replies.author: LatentBlade
replies.body: I think slop has become an over used term but you are using it correctly. These tools should be multipliers, not shortcuts.

comments.author: Southern_Charge5794
comments.body:
I am developer with more than 20 years of experience and wanted to raise my scepticism about it. AI is good at short iterations and is not a silver bullet.   
It saves a lot of time but quality of code is better than one year ago but not production ready and has a lot of mess.   
For example after weeks of learning Godot I have automated QA process, where you write unit tests first, do visual QA and shows output logs.  
At this time I am working on asset creation where I create or use existing enemy assets, approves it in a chat and run animation creation to make it pixel perfect and stunning. But I need to validate it anyway, otherwise it will be AI slop with low effort.

replies.author: SBelwas
replies.body: I guess I'm trying to get to the point where I can spend more time up front, spec out systems, noodle on things, get inspiration for assets etc then launch monitor from afar with designated things that require a human in the loop sit down to refine and verify that things look okay because I dont want things to be slop at all and im totally willing to not do this i just was curious if anyone had succeeded getting decent output but having longer periods where things go more autonomously. Sounds like it might be far off or intractible

replies.author: Southern_Charge5794
replies.body:
My current goal is to not switch from my favourite editor to googling, different image generation services and etc and it sounds similar.   
Try something small and share your experience.

replies.author: d-czar
replies.body: This is totally what I do and it’s not only super fast and productive if you know how to use AI (planning mode helps a tone, as do Unit tests and live smoke tests) — but it’s also a lot of fun because it removes a lot of tedium from coding. People who call everything slop just don’t know what’s possible know. Every coder who knows anything heavily used AI at this point, it’s 100x more productive.  The skill is knowjng how to guide it and refine it. This argument is very 2024 guys.  It’s just kind of silly now. We should be talking about the best ways to use it, success stories, tools etc.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body:
Im using Godot and have been using codex to help with just my scripts. 

I’m making a fairly simple 2-d game and have had no issues I couldn’t fix so far. Id say the game has the complexity of maybe something like Super Metroid or Hollow Knight if you are familiar with those games. I feel like the systems are maybe 3/4 done and are working as expected.

I’d love to get some pointers from you on what pitfalls I might run into either having codex mostly generate my scripts for me. 

I don’t let cursor do anything else but scripts. I set up nodes, signals, scenes, inspector parameters and all that stuff manually. 

I keep my scripts somewhat organized but I do fear a point that there will be an issue with my project that I won’t be able to fix.

replies.author: Southern_Charge5794
replies.body: Why scripts only? My main struggle with codex or cursor is that they not following you and I am trying to fix that using skills, otherwise you will get very hard to read code

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: I’ve only been doing scripts with cursor, partially so I can learn Godot better by doing things myself and also so I can understand my project better. When I’m closer to complete I’ll probably yolo and let cursor have full access to Godot.
